source_text: Nam cum tales ascribis operi Dei, quales facere non potest, ostendis nihil ad Deum, id quod ab eo dixeras fieri, pertinere.
pass_a_gloss: For when you ascribe to the work of God such as he cannot make, you show that what you had said is done by him pertains nothing to God.
pass_b_english: For when you attribute to God’s work the kind of beings he cannot make, you show that what you said he makes has nothing to do with God.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at this locus; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
